| −2.6 | 0.0027 | 1.5% | 0.12% | 0 |
| −2.7 | 0.0029 | 3.7% | 0.6% | 0.02% |
| −2.8 | 0.0032 | 7.2% | 2.2% | 0.05% |
| −2.9 | 0.0035 | 13% | 5.5% | 0.6% |

These rest on an assumed cost factor of 1.09 per 0.1 of gain. `ins_only(-2.8)` is now saved: only the output columns changed, and the transition table is original.

I will measure −2.8 directly on tu0 (2020000100..199), the costliest batch at 0.00428 for −2.6, to get the real factor. Scaling predicts about 0.0051 there. A clearly lower result (say ≤0.0047) would mean the risks above are overstated. A result at or above 0.0051 would support settling on a gain between −2.6 and −2.7.
